scope: Finite theory-level redefinition audit. The transformations act on descriptions of Q-side free valuation bits and map lift laws to lift laws. They are not silently added to AP3G as in-model gauge.

interpretive_boundary.full_group_status: candidate theory-level field-redefinition group, not existing gauge
interpretive_boundary.why_gauge_status_is_unsettled: It changes valuation contents q_v in trace-dependent sectors; AP3G currently treats context and valuation as part of mode identity.
interpretive_boundary.component_effect: The redefinition maps one lift law to another while P-side theta labels can remain fixed. It does not by itself derive a unique physical/component interpretation.

restricted_conclusion: The 16 trace-preserving lifts form one orbit under full sector-dependent Q-coordinate redefinitions, and eight orbits under a uniform global complement. Thus lift multiplicity can be treated as a field- redefinition torsor only if an additional gauge/redundancy principle is justified. Existing AP3G gauge does not do this, so no privileged lift is derived and no valuation-changing redefinition may yet be reported as physical redundancy.
